quote: Lemma 1. Let X and Y be the random vectors as given in (5) [X ∼ NVMMd(µ, Σ, λ, h), Y ∼ NVMMd(µ′, Σ′, λ′, h)]. If µ ≤ µ′, λ ≤ λ′, σ = σ′, σij ≤ σij′ for all 1 ≤ i, j ≤ d, then P(X ≥ t) ≤ P(Y ≥ t) for all t ∈ Rd. If µi < µ′i or λi < λ′i for some i or σij < σij′ for some (i, j), then the above inequality is in fact strict.
family: normal mean-variance mixture NMVM_d(µ, Σ, λ, h): X|W ~ Nd(µ + Wλ, WΣ), W ~ h mixing distribution (includes generalized hyperbolic submodels)
compared: X vs Y under componentwise ordering of location, skewness parameter and covariances

hypotheses.text: µ ≤ µ′, λ ≤ λ′, σ = σ′, σij ≤ σij′ for all i, j

conclusion.direction: P(X ≥ t) <= P(Y ≥ t) for all t (strict if some inequality strict) — Slepian-type inequality

quote: Lemma 2. Let X and Y be the random vectors as given in (5) and ϕp(.|w) = ϕd(.; µp + wλp, wΣp), 0 ≤ p ≤ 1, where µp = pµ + (1−p)µ′, λp = pλ + (1−p)λ′, Σp = pΣ + (1−p)Σ′. Further, let f : Rd → R be twice continuously differentiable and, for any w ∈ SH, satisfy the following conditions (i)-(iii) [boundary limits vanish]. If the following conditions Σi(µ′i − µi) ∂f/∂xi ≥ 0, Σi(λ′i − λi) ∂f/∂xi ≥ 0, ΣiΣj(σ′ij − σij) ∂²f/∂xi∂xj ≥ 0 hold, then E(f(X)) ≤ E(f(Y)).
compared: X vs Y under integral-order generator conditions (sign of directional derivatives of f in direction of parameter differences)

Σi(µ′i − µi) ∂f/∂xi ≥ 0; Σi(λ′i − λi) ∂f/∂xi ≥ 0; Σij(σ′ij − σij) ∂²f/∂xi∂xj ≥ 0

conclusion.direction: E f(X) <= E f(Y)

quote: Lemma 5. Let X1 and X2 be two SSMSN random variables given by Xi|τ ∼ SN1(µi, a1(τ1)σi², a2(τ)αi), i = 1, 2. Then, X1 ≼st X2 if and only if µ1 ≤ µ2, σ1 = σ2 and α1 ≤ α2 (λτ,1 ≤ λτ,2).

hypotheses.text: µ1 ≤ µ2, σ1 = σ2 and α1 ≤ α2 (λτ,1 ≤ λτ,2)

conclusion.direction: X1 <=st X2 iff the conditions hold

quote: To illustrate the result of Lemma 5, the survival functions for two special cases of univariate SSMSN distributions are plotted in Figure 1: (i) the skew-t-normal distributions denoted by STN(µ, σ, α, ν), and (ii) the skew-Cauchy distribution denoted by SC(µ, σ, α). Distributions whose parameters satisfy the conditions of Lemma 5 are stochastically ordered. Otherwise, their survival functions intersect each other and are therefore not stochastically ordered.
family: skew-t-normal STN(µ, σ, α, ν) and skew-Cauchy SC(µ, σ, α)

quote: Lemma 6. Let X1 and X2 be the random variables as given in (21) [Xi ∼ NVMM1(µi, σi², λi, h)]. (i) If µ1 = µ2, then X1 ≼st X2 if and only if σ1 = σ2 and λ1 ≤ λ2; (ii) If λ1 = λ2, then X1 ≼st X2 if and only if σ1 = σ2 and µ1 ≤ µ2.
compared: X1 vs X2; iff characterizations under one common parameter

conclusion.direction: (i) X1 <=st X2 iff σ1 = σ2 and λ1 <= λ2; (ii) iff σ1 = σ2 and µ1 <= µ2
